newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-KENT BATSMEN INSPIRED BY WAUGH CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-KENT BATSMEN INSPIRED BY WAUGH CENTURY.

text.p: The three top Kent batsmen who fell for ducks on Saturday bounced back on Sunday as the county championship leaders made a fight of it on the second day of their three-day match against Australia.
Trevor Ward, Ed Smith and Alan Wells all fell victim to paceman Mike Kasprowicz on the opening morning but found their form with 68, 46, and 65 respectively as Kent reached 234 for five at close.
That was a deficit of 114 after the tourists, led by a brilliant 154 from Steve Waugh, reached 315 all out from their overnight 207 for five.

Waugh completed his fourth hundred of the tour after resuming from his overnight 96 and, despite struggling with a hand injury, said he will be fit for the final test against England which starts at the Oval on Thursday.
Michael Bevan contributed 55 before becoming one of three victims in 17 balls for young Kent bowler Ben Phillips.
